title: Beinn Edra Fortress Memorial
squadron: USAAF (en route USA to Italy via Iceland)

external_narratives.summary: B-17G serial 44-83325 crashed into Beinn Edra on the Isle of Skye on 3 March 1945 during a ferry flight from Meeks Field, Iceland to RAF Valley, Anglesey. The brand-new aircraft flew into thick cloud concealing the mountain, killing all nine crew.

memorial_details:
Name: Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress 44-83325
Type: Board / Plaque / Tablet
Description: Dark metal sign attached to posts.
Inscription: This site is dedicated to the brave crew of the B-17 who perished here/ during WW2 on March 3, 1945./ They selflessly gave their lives so others could be free./ There is no greater act of love. May they rest in peace./ Crew of 44-83325:/ [crew names inscribed on memorial]/ This memorial was placed by the families of the fallen servicemen
Location: The plane crashed on the Trotternish Ridge on the Scottish isle of Skye on a peak named Beinn Edra. The marker is located at the base of the Beinn Edra peak and the beginning of an aircraft wreckage field. Beinn Edra Skye And Lochalsh Highlands and Islands IV51 9LB Scotland
Grid Ref: NG 45670 63169
Coordinates: 57.586689000000,-6.257013000000

The inscription reads: 'This site is dedicated to the brave crew of the B-17 who perished here/during WW2 on March 3, 1945./They selflessly gave their lives so others could be free./There is no greater act of love.

May they rest in peace./Crew of 44-83325:/[crew names inscribed on memorial]/This memorial was placed by the families of the fallen servicemen'.

The memorial was established by the families of the fallen servicemen.
narrative: The crew of a B-17G Flying Fortress, under the command of 1st Lieutenant Paul M. Overfield, were ferrying their aircraft from the United States to Italy via Iceland when they encountered heavy cloud over the Scottish Highlands. Flying blind in the deteriorating conditions, the aircraft struck the slopes of Beinn Edra with catastrophic force. All nine men aboard were killed: 1st Lieutenant Overfield, 2nd Lieutenant Leroy Elmer Cagle, 2nd Lieutenant Charles K. Jeanblanc, Corporal Carter D. Wilkinson, Corporal Harold Duane Blue, Corporal Harold A. Fahselt, Corporal Arthur W. Kopp Jr, Corporal George S. Aldrich, and Corporal John H. Vaughan. None of the crew survived. Wreckage from the aircraft remains scattered across the hillside, marking the place where nine American airmen lost their lives before ever reaching their theatre of war.
